description:
The existing `erased_closure_dnf_hygiene` tests use capture-free branded closures. They remain valid coverage of interner idempotence: erasing the joined descriptor removes both brands in place, produces duplicate bare-arrow clauses, and relies on `Types::intern` to collapse them. Disabling funcs-axis `dedupe_exact_clauses` makes both existing tests fail, so the zero-capture case does not bypass the `A ∨ A` hazard.

fz-kdt.127 introduced another erasure result: capture-bearing closures retain their capture types in an anonymous closure literal. Existing tests compare separately erased arms, but no test carries two such brands through union and erasure together.

Add a capture-bearing case or twin proving:

- The pre-erasure union has two funcs clauses.
- Erasure leaves one funcs clause.
- The surviving clause is anonymous and retains the expected capture type.
- The erased union is the same `Ty` as either separately erased arm.
- Their activation keys are equal.

For red-first evidence, disable funcs-axis exact-clause deduplication and show the new test fails. Do not require the existing zero-capture test to remain green; it correctly fails too.

This is coverage work, not a current behavior defect.
title: Extend erased-closure DNF hygiene coverage to capture-bearing anonymous literals
